findings.body:
**`reviewStateOfDecision` maps `reviewDecision: ""` to `unknown`. It should map to `none`.**

The doc comment at Lines 314-322 says an explicit `null` means no review policy, and the code at Line 327 matches only `null`. `gh pr view --json reviewDecision` does not print `null` for that case. It prints an empty string. An independent project reports that `gh pr view --json` serializes GraphQL null as `""`. The GitHub community thread shows the same `{ "reviewDecision": "" }` output.

A PR in a repo with no review requirement therefore returns `{ state: 'unknown' }`. That state is not the intended `none`. The doc comment says the fold treats `unknown` fail-closed, so such PRs probably never reach a ready verdict. This repo's own R2 policy sets `required_approving_review_count` to 0 (single-owner flow), so this is a realistic production shape. I did not see the fold code, so the exact downstream effect is unconfirmed.

Add an empty-string match. Keep a missing key as `unknown`.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  if (decision === null) return { state: 'none' };
+  if (decision === null || decision === '') return { state: 'none' };
```
</details>

Add a fixture for `reviewDecision: ""` to the test in `test/ops/pr/registry.test.ts`. The module header says the parsers are tested against captured gh JSON shapes, so a captured payload with the empty string would catch this.
findings.title: `reviewStateOfDecision` maps `reviewDecision: ""` to `unknown`. It should map to `none`.

findings.body:
**Reject glob refspecs in the `push` guard. `refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` bypasses the protected-branch check.**

`safeArgs` passes `push origin refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*`:
- Line 203: `colon > 0` and the destination is not the last character, so the refspec counts as an explicit non-empty `src:dst`.
- Line 213: `isProtectedRef` compares the destination `refs/heads/*` to `main` by string equality only.
- Git expands the glob on push and updates `main`.

The doc on Lines 86-117 presents the allowlist as closing push bypasses. The same gap exists for the partial-name alias `heads/main`, which git resolves to `refs/heads/main`.

Refuse glob metacharacters in push refspecs. Treat `heads/<branch>` as protected too.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-        if (isProtectedRef(pushDestination(refspec), protectedBranch)) {
+        if (/[*?[\\]/.test(refspec)) {
+          throw new UnsafeMergeArgsError(
+            args,
+            `push refspec ${JSON.stringify(refspec)} contains a glob — wildcard pushes can reach the protected branch`,
+          );
+        }
+        if (isProtectedRef(pushDestination(refspec), protectedBranch)) {
```

And in `isProtectedRef` (Lines 82-83):

```diff
-  ref === protectedBranch || ref === `refs/heads/${protectedBranch}`;
+  ref === protectedBranch ||
+  ref === `refs/heads/${protectedBranch}` ||
+  ref === `heads/${protectedBranch}`;
```
</details>
findings.title: Reject glob refspecs in the `push` guard. `refs/heads/:refs/heads/` bypasses the protected-branch check.

findings.body:
**Apply the flag-free and glob rules to the `fetch` shape.**

The `push` and `worktree` shapes refuse `-`-prefixed tokens (round 3). The `fetch` branch does not:
- `fetch origin --upload-pack=<cmd>` passes. The flag has no `:`, so the loop skips it.
- `fetch --upload-pack=<cmd> origin x` passes. The flag lands in the remote slot.
- `fetch origin +refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` passes. The destination `refs/heads/*` does not equal the protected branch, so the force-update of `main` is not detected.

`fetchRef` always builds `+ref:ref`, so the real implementation does not hit this today. The guard is meant to be the allowlist, so it should refuse these shapes itself.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       const tail = rest.slice(1);
       if (tail.length < 2) throw unknown(); // remote + ≥1 refspec
+      for (const arg of tail) {
+        if (arg.startsWith('-') || /[*?[\\]/.test(arg)) {
+          throw new UnsafeMergeArgsError(
+            args,
+            `flags and globs are not part of the documented fetch shape — refused ${JSON.stringify(arg)}`,
+          );
+        }
+      }
```
</details>
findings.title: Apply the flag-free and glob rules to the `fetch` shape.
